title: Amar Upadhyay Returns as Mihir Virani in Kyunki 2 After 14-Week Absence That Sank Ratings
excerpt: The actor's exit dropped the show from No. 1 to No. 5 on the charts. After fee negotiations and a massive fan campaign, Mihir is back in Shanti Niketan.
body:
• Amar Upadhyay has returned to Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi 2 as Mihir Virani after a 14-week absence that saw the show's ratings drop from the No. 1 to No. 5 position.
  • The actor says "Mihir has evolved with time" and describes stepping back onto the Shanti Niketan set as "incredibly special."
  • His return follows reported fee negotiations with the show's producers — Upadhyay reportedly charges around Rs 1.5 lakh per episode — after a massive fan campaign demanding Mihir's comeback.
  • Kyunki 2, produced by Ekta Kapoor and starring Smriti Irani as Tulsi Virani, premiered in July 2025 and has clocked over 1.6 billion views.
https://youtube.com/watch?v=di8tDqo4tDE

Mihir Virani is back in Shanti Niketan. Actor Amar Upadhyay has returned to Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi 2 after a 14-week absence that tested both the show's ratings and the patience of millions of viewers who grew up watching the original series.

"Stepping back onto the set felt incredibly special," Upadhyay told The Times of India in an exclusive interview. "Mihir isn't coming back as the same person. He has evolved with time."

The Exit That Shook Ratings

Upadhyay's departure from the show on May 3 triggered an immediate and measurable decline. Kyunki 2, which had held the No. 1 spot on the television ratings charts with Mihir as part of the storyline, slipped to No. 5 within weeks. The drop was significant enough to reignite debate about the enduring pull of legacy characters in Indian television.

https://x.com/GossipsTv/status/2087425001352008006

Fans did not take the absence quietly. On Instagram, fan pages, and online forums, viewers mounted a sustained campaign demanding Mihir's return — echoing the historic audience reaction in the original series when the character was written out in the early 2000s. "Mihir is the male lead and one of the pillars of this story," one fan wrote. "His prolonged absence is not only hurting the narrative but also disconnecting viewers from the show."

Behind the Scenes: Fee Negotiations

The 14-week gap was not entirely a creative decision. Reports indicate that Upadhyay's return was delayed by fee negotiations with the show's producers at Balaji Telefilms. According to multiple entertainment outlets, the actor reportedly charges around Rs 1.5 lakh per episode, making him one of the highest-paid actors in the second season. Lead actress Smriti Irani is reportedly being paid approximately Rs 14 lakh per episode, though neither figure has been officially confirmed.

The production team approached Upadhyay again after the show's recent 10-year time leap, which saw Tulsi returning to the Virani household from prison. With the storyline clearly setting the stage for Mihir's re-entry, both sides ultimately reached an agreement.

"When I got the call for Mihir, I couldn't believe it. I thought it was some prank call. The first thing I asked was if Smriti Irani will be back as Tulsi, and they said yes."

— Amar Upadhyay

A Show Built on Nostalgia — and Delivering

Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi 2 premiered on July 29, 2025, marking the 25th anniversary of the original series that ran from 2000 to 2008 and became one of the most-watched shows in Indian television history. Produced by Ekta Kapoor, the reboot brought back Smriti Irani as Tulsi and Upadhyay as Mihir, along with returning cast members including Mouni Roy, Karishma Tanna, and veteran actor Jeetendra.

The show's launch was a cultural event — it clocked 1.6 billion views in its opening week and quickly topped both television and OTT charts. The series is designed as a limited run, needing 150 episodes to reach the 2,000-episode milestone from the original's run.

What's Next for Mihir

Upadhyay has hinted that Mihir's return will bring significant changes to the storyline. The character, long regarded as the "green flag" of Indian television for his supportive relationship with Tulsi, will reportedly navigate a transformed Virani household following the decade-long time jump.

The Tulsi-Mihir dynamic, fondly known as "Tuhir" by fans, has been one of the most celebrated on-screen pairings in Indian television. With both actors back on set, the show appears positioned to reclaim the ratings ground it lost during Mihir's absence.
nri_angle: Kyunki remains a touchstone for the Indian diaspora — the original series was a shared cultural experience across NRI households, and the reboot is drawing the same cross-generational audience.
